note: Ten contested rows from the 35-prompt shadow run. Each records which reader was right and why, and — more usefully — what kind of defect it is. Three kinds appeared, and they need three different fixes.

rows.why: 'Each month I hold whichever ... had the best 12-month return, past 5 years.' The window is the past 5 years; 'each month' is a rebalancing cadence, not a window modifier. The compiler's ROLLING detector still reads cadence+window as many windows — the same class as the cadence/window collision closed earlier, and evidence it was not fully closed.
Same shape: 'Each month I sell ... past 5 years.'
'... increase it with inflation each year after, past 5 years.'
'... each year starting at age 73, past 5 years.'

'I hold 60% VTI and 40% BND ...' — the sentence names both and the model reported one. A recall miss on the dimension where a miss is most expensive: a portfolio read as one holding is not the portfolio described. This is the clearest single argument against treating the hosted reader as authoritative without a comparator.

rows.model: US stocks, international stocks or bonds
rows.correct: US stocks, international stocks or bonds
rows.why: The compiler truncated a three-way description to the first token. 'US' is not a holding, and a plan built on it would price something nobody described.

rows.model: the 500 largest US companies individually rather than through an ETF
rows.correct: the 500 largest US companies individually rather than through an ETF
rows.why: The compiler picked two nouns out of a sentence that explicitly rejects the ETF route. Reading 'ETF' out of 'rather than through an ETF' is the inversion a regex cannot see.
The watched series is the index, and 'ETF' is the wrapper the user buys. Naming the wrapper as the observed series is the defect that made a plan evaluate its condition on the wrong instrument.

'Convert enough of my traditional IRA to a Roth' names two accounts, and `account_type` holds one. Both readers are reporting a true fact about the sentence and the schema forces them to disagree. A conversion needs a source and a destination, and until the schema has them this row is not adjudicable — recorded as such rather than resolved by preferring a reader.

summary.reading: Eight of ten contested rows are legacy-reader defects, one is a model recall miss, and one is unanswerable because the schema cannot represent the sentence. That is the shape a shadow phase is supposed to produce: most disagreements teach you about the thing being replaced, one teaches you about the replacement, and the residue teaches you about your own instrument.

classes.why: One class, not 25 findings. The compiler extracts capitalised nouns as if they were instruments — 'ETF' read out of 'US value ETF', 'US' and 'EM' out of 'US and Developed and EM' — which is a category error: ETF is a wrapper, not a holding, and a plan priced on it would price nothing the user named. The model reports the phrase the sentence actually uses ('core index fund', 'multi-asset ETF set'), which is faithful but not resolvable to a series either.
classes.and_the_model_too: WM-0025 describes two sleeves — a core index fund and a 30% US value ETF satellite — and the model reported only the core. So on multi-sleeve descriptions both readers are incomplete, in different ways. Neither is safe to trust alone on the dimension where being wrong is most expensive.
classes.what_it_argues_for: `assets` needs structure the schema does not have: a list of sleeves, each with a description and an optional weight. A single string cannot hold 'a core fund plus a 30% satellite', so both readers are being asked a question that has no correct single answer — the same shape as the account_type conversion gap, one dimension over.

classes.why: The same cadence-plus-window misread already adjudicated on the 35: 120 agree, 15 contested, 9 compiler-only, and zero model-only. The direction is uniform, which is what makes it a defect in one reader rather than a disagreement between two.

one_sided.reading: Ten to one, and the largest buckets are dimensions the legacy compiler has no concept of at all: objective 116, sell_action 49, allocation_method 32, stated_weights 23. That is the recall gap Discovery exists to close, measured rather than asserted. The 33 compiler-only readings are the reader-defect candidates and are small enough to inspect by hand.
